prompt: Stage 3-2, level 6, 71 HP, alternating wins and losses. You hold four components on the bench: two defensive, one AD, one AP. None of the pairs is the perfect item for the 4-cost carry you hope to find at 4-2. Your 2-star 2-cost tank and 2-star 3-cost carry are both naked. What do you do with the components?

options.label: Slam two items now: the two defensive components into a tank item on the 2-cost tank, and AD + AP into a damage item on the 3-cost carry
Hold all four: the perfect items for the 4-cost carry are worth waiting for, and 71 HP is fine
Slam only the tank item and keep AD and AP for the carry you will find at 4-2

explanation:
By 3-2 you want two completed items on the board. A completed item is worth far more than the two components that made it: the components on the bench add zero to the fight, and the item adds a full stat line to a unit that is fighting now. Two defensive components on the 2-star tank in the centre make the front line hold; AD + AP on the 2-star 3-cost carry is not a perfect item, but a mixed damage item on the unit doing your damage still wins fights that a naked carry loses.

'Perfect items for the 4-cost' is the trap: that carry is at 4-2 at the earliest, two rounds and a level away, and only if you find him. Between now and then there are three fights, and the 3-4 carousel and the 3-7 monster round will hand you more components. A 4-cost carry with two good items beats a 4-cost with two perfect items and 20 less HP behind him. Slamming only the tank item halves the benefit for the same reason. Two items by 3-2, on the units you have.
principle: Two completed items on the board by 3-2. A component on the bench has a value of zero in every fight it sits out.
commonMistake: Holding components for a carry who is not on the board yet, and losing three fights with a naked carry and a naked tank.
hint: Count how many fights happen before 4-2 and what each of the four components contributes to them while on the bench.
